newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Dubinin says favours smaller Eurobonds, more often.
newsitem.headline: Dubinin says favours smaller Eurobonds, more often.

text.p: Russia's Central Bank Chairman Sergei Dubinin said on Tuesday that Russia should make more frequent, but smaller Eurobond issues to push the price down.
"Significant demand for Russian paper allows to place bigger volumes than we have now, but we should try to cut prices," Dubinin told a meeting of senior Finance Ministry officials.
"By our estimates, we could consider cutting the volumes, but increasing the number of issues."

Russia placed a debut $1 billion Eurobond in November. In March it was followed by a two billion mark Eurobond. In the second half of June it plans to issue another dollar-denominated Eurobond and the Finance Ministry has said the volume will be comparable to the first two issues.
Russia plans to issue one more Eurobond in autumn.
